label: Programming model v2
description: Confirms the project uses the Azure Functions Python v2 decorator-based programming model (via @app. or @bp. decorators).
hint: Use func.FunctionApp() and decorator-based triggers such as @app.route().

label: Blueprint registration
description: Warns when a Blueprint has decorators but is never registered on the FunctionApp.
hint: Register each Blueprint with app.register_functions(bp) so its decorators are indexed at runtime.

label: Python version
description: Checks that the target Python version is a supported Azure Functions runtime (3.10–3.14).
hint: Target a Python version supported by Azure Functions: 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, or 3.14.
source_title: Azure Functions Python developer guide — Supported Python versions
why_it_matters: Azure Functions supports only Python 3.10–3.14. Targeting an older interpreter (≤ 3.9) or a version newer than the runtime supports causes deployment failures and unsupported runtime errors.
symptoms: Deployment fails with 'Python version not supported'; functions fail to start; a too-new interpreter is silently downgraded or rejected by the host.

label: Python runtime lifecycle
description: Checks the target Python version against its published Azure Functions end-of-support date, warning on a retiring runtime and failing on one past end-of-support.
hint: Target a Python version with a long support runway. Upgrade a retiring runtime before its Azure Functions end-of-support date.
source_title: Azure Functions — Supported languages (Python runtime lifecycle)
why_it_matters: Azure Functions retires Python runtimes on a published schedule. Deploying on a runtime at or past end-of-support risks losing security updates and, eventually, the ability to deploy at all.
symptoms: Deployments on a retiring runtime keep working until the end-of-support date, then fail or lose patching; upgrades left too late force a rushed migration.

label: Functions runtime lifecycle
description: Checks the Azure Functions runtime major version (FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION) for a Python app: v1 is incompatible with Python, v2/v3 are out of support, v3 on Linux Consumption stops running on a published date, and v4 is the current GA runtime.
hint: Target the v4 Azure Functions runtime (FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION=~4). The v1/v2/v3 runtimes are legacy or out of support; v1 does not support Python at all.
source_title: Azure Functions — Compare runtime versions (runtime lifecycle)
why_it_matters: Running on a legacy or out-of-support Azure Functions runtime loses security updates and eventually the ability to run; runtime v1 cannot host a Python app at all.
symptoms: Host fails to start on an unsupported runtime; v3 Linux Consumption apps stop running after the published date; v1 rejects Python apps outright.

label: Hosting plan lifecycle
description: Checks the resolved hosting plan against its published retirement date, informing on a distant retirement, warning inside the retiring-soon window, and failing once the plan has retired.
hint: Linux Consumption is retiring; consider Flex Consumption for new Python workloads.
source_title: Azure Functions — Migrate Consumption to Flex Consumption (hosting plan lifecycle)
why_it_matters: Hosting plans retire on a published schedule; an app left on a retiring plan must eventually migrate or stop running.
symptoms: Apps on a retiring hosting plan keep running until the retirement date, then must migrate; migrations left too late force a rushed move.

label: Flex Consumption runtime config
description: For a Flex Consumption app, validates the runtime declared under functionAppConfig.runtime (name/version) against the supported Python versions, and warns when a legacy linuxFxVersion is present (Flex ignores it).
hint: Declare the Flex Consumption runtime under functionAppConfig.runtime (name/version); do not use linuxFxVersion.
why_it_matters: Flex Consumption resolves its runtime from functionAppConfig.runtime and ignores linuxFxVersion; a misdeclared or unsupported runtime version fails to deploy or run.
symptoms: A Flex app with only linuxFxVersion set has no effective runtime declaration; an unsupported Python version is rejected at deploy time.

label: Flex Consumption deprecated app settings
description: For a Flex Consumption app, warns when legacy app settings that Flex ignores are declared (worker-runtime selection, Oryx/remote-build toggles, Azure Files content-share settings, run-from-package, and VNet route-all), citing the replacement mechanism for each.
hint: Remove legacy app settings on Flex Consumption; configure the runtime, deployment, scaling, and networking through functionAppConfig and site networking properties instead.
source_title: Azure Functions — App settings reference (Flex Consumption plan deprecations)
why_it_matters: Flex Consumption ignores a set of legacy app settings; leaving them in place is a configuration smell that masks the correct functionAppConfig-based configuration and can confuse deployments.
symptoms: Deprecated app settings are silently ignored on Flex Consumption, so settings such as FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME or WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE have no effect and hide the real configuration.

label: Flex Consumption deployment storage
description: For a Flex Consumption app, validates the deployment storage shape declared under functionAppConfig.deployment.storage: a container URL must be specified and authentication must be configured (managed identity or a named storage account connection string). Skips gracefully when infra declares no deployment storage block.
hint: Declare a blob container under functionAppConfig.deployment.storage with a value URL and authentication (managed identity or a named connection string).
why_it_matters: Flex Consumption deploys from a blob container declared under functionAppConfig.deployment.storage; a missing container or unconfigured authentication produces a deployment that cannot fetch its package.
symptoms: A Flex app with no deployment container or no authentication configured fails to deploy or cannot fetch its package at scale-out.

label: Binding connection resolution
description: Extracts connection= references from v2 trigger/binding decorators (Storage, Service Bus, Event Hub, Cosmos DB, and any binding exposing a connection keyword) and resolves each against local.settings.json Values plus ingested deploy-config app settings. Warns when a referenced connection has no corresponding configuration; identity-based connection groups (<name>__...) are treated as configured.
hint: Add the missing app setting for each referenced connection, or configure an identity-based connection group (<name>__serviceUri / <name>__accountName).
why_it_matters: A trigger or binding that references connection="Name" fails to bind at runtime when no matching app setting or identity-based connection group is configured; catching this before deploy avoids a cold-start failure discovered only in production logs.
symptoms: A binding references a connection name that has no corresponding app setting, so the function fails to start or the trigger never fires after deployment.

label: Virtual environment
description: Checks if a virtual environment is activated (venv, conda, or uv).
hint: Create and activate a virtual environment (e.g. 'python -m venv .venv' then 'source .venv/bin/activate'). Both '.venv' and 'venv' directories are recognized and excluded from project scans.

label: Python executable
description: Checks if the Python executable path exists.
hint: Ensure Python is installed and sys.executable points to a valid path.

label: requirements.txt
description: Checks that dependencies are declared for the deployment mode: requirements.txt for remote build, or pyproject.toml for a local/prebuilt build.
hint: Azure remote build installs from requirements.txt, so add one (e.g. 'pip freeze > requirements.txt'). pyproject.toml alone is sufficient only for local/prebuilt deployments (--deployment-mode local).
source_title: Azure Functions Python developer guide — Managing dependencies
why_it_matters: Azure Functions performs a remote build by default and installs dependencies from requirements.txt; it never reads pyproject.toml. A pyproject-only project passes locally but fails at deploy time unless it uses a local/prebuilt deployment.
symptoms: ModuleNotFoundError at runtime; deployment pipeline fails with missing package errors; cold start crashes.

label: azure-functions package
description: Checks that the azure-functions package is installable for the deployment mode (requirements.txt for remote build, pyproject.toml for local/prebuilt).
hint: Add azure-functions to requirements.txt (Azure remote build installs from it). pyproject.toml alone suffices only for local/prebuilt deployments (--deployment-mode local).
why_it_matters: The azure-functions SDK is the binding between user code and the Functions host. Without it, triggers and bindings cannot be parsed and the app will not start.
symptoms: ImportError for azure.functions; function app fails to load; no triggers are registered.

label: Native dependency risk
description: Warns when requirements.txt includes packages with native extensions that often require platform-matching Linux builds.
hint: If you deploy native-extension packages, build against the Azure Functions Linux runtime. Prefer remote build with `func azure functionapp publish --build remote`.

label: azure-functions-worker not pinned
description: Warns if azure-functions-worker is directly declared in requirements.txt. The Azure Functions platform manages the worker runtime; pinning it can cause deployment failures.
hint: Remove azure-functions-worker from requirements.txt. The Azure Functions platform manages the worker runtime automatically.

label: host.json
description: Checks if host.json exists at the project root.
hint: Add host.json to configure the Azure Functions host runtime.
why_it_matters: host.json is required by the Azure Functions runtime to configure the host process. Without it the function app cannot start.
symptoms: Function app fails to start locally or in Azure; 'Missing host.json' error in logs.

label: host.json version
description: Checks that host.json declares "version": "2.0" as required by the v2 runtime.
hint: Add or correct "version": "2.0" in host.json.
why_it_matters: The runtime version field gates which host features are enabled. An incorrect or missing version causes the host to fall back to v1 behaviour or refuse to start.
symptoms: Runtime version mismatch errors; unexpected v1-style function loading; host startup failure.

label: local.settings.json
description: Checks if local.settings.json exists for local development.
hint: Create local.settings.json for local development if needed.

label: Azure Functions Core Tools (func)
description: Checks if Azure Functions Core Tools is available on PATH.
hint: Install Azure Functions Core Tools for local development and testing.

label: Azure Functions Core Tools version
description: Checks if Azure Functions Core Tools meets the minimum supported version.
hint: Install or upgrade Azure Functions Core Tools v4 for local development.

label: Durable Functions configuration
description: Checks for durableTask configuration in host.json when durable functions are present.
hint: If using Durable Functions, ensure durableTask settings are configured in host.json.

label: Application Insights configuration
description: Checks that Application Insights uses a connection string (instrumentation-key ingestion ended 2025-03-31).
hint: Set APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING (instrumentation keys are retired). Optionally set APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_AUTHENTICATION_STRING for Entra (AAD) auth.

label: extensionBundle
description: Checks whether extensionBundle is configured in host.json.
hint: Use extensionBundle to ensure required extensions are available for bindings.

label: ASGI/WSGI compatibility
description: Detects whether the project exposes an ASGI or WSGI callable.
hint: Verify that any ASGI or WSGI app is exposed as expected for the Functions host.

label: Detect unused or invalid files
description: Detects common unwanted files in the project root or deployment package.
hint: Remove or exclude unwanted files from deployment to reduce package size and avoid accidental secrets.

label: .funcignore
description: Checks if a .funcignore file is present to control what gets deployed.
hint: Add a .funcignore file to exclude test files, venv, and other non-deployment assets.

label: local.settings.json not git-tracked
description: Checks that local.settings.json is not tracked by git, which could expose secrets in version control.
hint: Add local.settings.json to .gitignore to prevent accidental secret exposure in version control.

label: extensionBundle v4 recommended
description: Checks that extensionBundle in host.json uses the recommended v4 version range [4.*, 5.0.0).
hint: Update extensionBundle in host.json to use id 'Microsoft.Azure.Functions.ExtensionBundle' with version '[4.*, 5.0.0)'.

label: Decorator order
description: Warns when @validate_http is stacked outside @with_context. The correct order (top to bottom) is @app.route -> @with_context -> @validate_http.
hint: Move @validate_http below (closer to def) @with_context so it wraps first.
why_it_matters: Inverted decorator order lets @with_context wrap last, discarding the endpoint metadata attached by @validate_http and breaking OpenAPI generation.
symptoms: Missing or empty endpoint metadata at runtime; OpenAPI schema omits validated routes.

label: Endpoint metadata coverage
description: Warns when HTTP route handlers in a project that depends on azure-functions-validation lack @validate_http, meaning they will not emit endpoint OpenAPI metadata.
hint: Add @validate_http to HTTP route handlers that should appear in the generated OpenAPI schema.
why_it_matters: Route handlers without @validate_http produce no endpoint metadata and stay invisible in auto-generated OpenAPI documentation.
symptoms: Endpoints missing from OpenAPI spec; incomplete API documentation.

label: OpenAPI version consistency
description: Warns when a project mixes OpenAPI 3.0 signals (3.0.x version strings or nullable keyword) with OpenAPI 3.1 signals (3.1.x version strings), which produces inconsistent generated specs.
hint: Standardise on a single OpenAPI version; avoid mixing 3.0 (nullable) and 3.1 constructs.
why_it_matters: Mixing OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 constructs yields a spec that some tooling cannot parse, breaking client generation and docs.
symptoms: OpenAPI tooling errors; nullable fields ignored or rejected; inconsistent schema output.

label: Endpoint scan before spec build
description: Warns when the OpenAPI spec is built before endpoints are scanned/registered, or when a spec is built without any endpoint scan, producing an empty or incomplete spec.
hint: Scan/register endpoints before building the OpenAPI spec (e.g. build_spec, get_openapi_json, generate_openapi_spec) so the generated document includes all routes.
why_it_matters: Building the spec before endpoints are discovered emits an empty or partial OpenAPI document, hiding routes from consumers.
symptoms: Generated OpenAPI spec missing endpoints; empty paths object.

label: LangGraph route authentication
description: Warns when a project that imports langgraph exposes HTTP routes with auth_level set to ANONYMOUS, leaving graph endpoints publicly reachable.
hint: Require authentication (e.g. AuthLevel.FUNCTION) for LangGraph HTTP routes.
why_it_matters: Anonymous LangGraph endpoints let anyone invoke expensive model/graph runs, risking cost abuse and data exposure.
symptoms: Unauthenticated access to graph endpoints; unexpected invocation costs.

label: Orchestrator determinism
description: Fails when orchestration or entity trigger functions call nondeterministic APIs (datetime.now, random, uuid, requests, open, os.getenv), which breaks Durable Functions replay.
hint: Move nondeterministic work (time, randomness, I/O) into activity functions; orchestrators must be deterministic.
why_it_matters: Durable Functions replay orchestrator code repeatedly; nondeterministic calls yield divergent replays and corrupt orchestration state.
symptoms: Non-deterministic orchestration failures; replay errors; inconsistent orchestration results.

label: OTel trace-context activation
description: Warns when a project opts into azure-functions-logging trace-context activation (activate_trace_context=True or set_default_trace_context_activation) but does not declare an opentelemetry dependency, so activation silently no-ops at runtime.
hint: Install the azure-functions-logging[otel] extra (or an opentelemetry-* package), or disable activate_trace_context.
why_it_matters: azure-functions-logging degrades trace-context activation to a no-op when OpenTelemetry is unavailable, so requested distributed tracing is silently dropped without any runtime error.
symptoms: Trace context never attaches to logs; spans missing from telemetry despite activation being enabled.

label: Functions extension version
description: Flags a missing, legacy, or non-~4 FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION in local.settings.json so the app targets the supported v4 Azure Functions runtime.
hint: Set FUNCTIONS_EXTENSION_VERSION to ~4 in local.settings.json; the v1/v2/v3 runtimes are retired.
why_it_matters: Legacy Azure Functions runtimes (~1/~2/~3) are retired; deploying against them causes host startup failures and unsupported-runtime errors.
symptoms: Host fails to start; deployment rejected with unsupported runtime version; functions never come online.

label: Linux runtime (linuxFxVersion)
description: Validates any Python linuxFxVersion declared in infra (bicep) config so Flex Consumption / Linux plan apps target a supported Python runtime.
hint: Set linuxFxVersion to a supported Python runtime (e.g. Python|3.12) in your infrastructure templates.
source_title: Azure Functions Python developer guide — Supported Python versions
why_it_matters: An unsupported Python runtime encoded in linuxFxVersion causes deployment or cold-start failures on Linux Consumption, Flex Consumption, Premium, and Dedicated plans.
symptoms: Deployment fails; app stuck in a restart loop; 'runtime not supported' errors in the platform logs.

label: host.json logLevel conflict
description: Flags host.json logging.logLevel category overrides that are more verbose than the configured default, which silently increases log volume, cost, and PII exposure.
hint: Align logging.logLevel category overrides with the intended default level in host.json, or raise the default deliberately.
why_it_matters: Category logLevel overrides win over default; a more-verbose category silently defeats a restrictive default, inflating Application Insights cost and risking PII in logs.
symptoms: Unexpectedly high log volume and telemetry cost; verbose logs in production despite a restrictive default level.

label: Dev-storage emulator connection
description: Flags AzureWebJobsStorage=UseDevelopmentStorage=true in deployable infra config (bicep/ARM), which points at the local Azurite emulator and must never ship to a deployed app.
hint: Provision a real storage account connection for AzureWebJobsStorage in deployment templates; keep UseDevelopmentStorage=true only in local.settings.json.
why_it_matters: The dev-storage emulator connection is unreachable from Azure; shipping it in provisioned app settings makes the deployed Functions host fail to start.
symptoms: Deployed app fails health checks; host cannot reach storage; triggers never fire in the cloud.

label: Pinned requirements
description: Warns when requirements.txt declares dependencies with no version specifier or an unbounded lower bound, making Azure remote-build deployments non-reproducible.
hint: Pin dependency versions (e.g. package==1.2.3) or add an upper bound to keep deployments reproducible.
why_it_matters: Azure remote build resolves requirements.txt at deploy time; unpinned dependencies let a new upstream release change or break a deployment without any code change.
symptoms: A deployment that previously worked suddenly fails or behaves differently; irreproducible builds across environments.
